The Examiner, Saturday, March 24, 1906• . _ the finishing touch. Half-time: Warrington, two goals two tries,Runcorn nil. With the aid of the wind Runcorn immediately made headway and after Allen had dribbled too near the line Berry saved his lines in fine style. Kenyon next placed the game at half way, but Runcorn responded well and Jolley scored cleverly with a fine drop kick. The Cestrians were generally on the aggressive and the defence of Berry was sorely tested. The game was carried on at high pressure,Run- corn displaying rare pertinacity continued the attack and Padbury succeeded in crossing. Another rush by the forwards ended in another try, whilst Walker also put on the finishing touch to a movement which was brimful of credit. Jolley added the goal, so that now the game had taken a complete change in favour of the Cestrians. Warrington retaliated, and Heath scoring a I try Preston added the goal, and the dual result was a draw, each side having registered 15 points. WARRING'IION "A " v. RADCLIFFE RANGERS. A large crowd assembled at Wilderspool on Saturday to witness this match, the re-appearance of Fish and Harris no doubt accounting forthe increased patronage. The Rangers have this season earned fame in winning the Manchester and District League Championship, and judging them on Saturday's performance they are one of the smartest junior teams which has opposed the combination champions this season. Having first advantage of the breeze the Rangers were early aggres- sive and eventually the visitors' full back placed a premier point from near half way. Both Fish and Harris were too well watched to become dangerous, and at half time the Radcliffe men led by two points. Turning round the Warringtonians were soon on the attack but found a resolute defence. In the last few minutes a movement was initated by Lambert and taken part in by Cartwright and Lloyd, which had a brilliant finish, the last named racing over near the posts. This was the winning point, for Knight failed to add the goal, and Warrington thus won by three points to two. STOCKTON HEATH TREE PLANTING. Mr. Whitley and the Parochial Committee. _ Amongst the minutes of the Stockton Heath Parochial Committee which were submitted for approval to the Runcorn Rural District Council on TuesdFly was one which read " That it be conveyed to the District Council that the statements made by Mr. Whitley at their meeting do not represent the views of the rate- payers or of this committee respecting the planting of trees in the village." The confirmation of the minutes had been moved and seconded when Mr. Whitley rose to move that the above minute be not approved. Mr. Woodward, who presided, pointed out that the District Council could not entertain the amendment as I the minute was only an expression of opinion. Mr. Whitley should discuss the matter with the Parochial Committee. Mr. Whitley: Am Ito be allowed to speak on the minute? Mr. Woodward : We cannot very well object to a proposition of this description. I think you must fight it out with the Parochial Committee, not here. Mr. Whitley: I maintain that never in the history of the District Council has such a shameful, scandalous and untruthful proposition as this been sent before the Council. The Chairman : We arc quite willing to accept your assurance. Mr. Whitley: I am sorry that the District Council should be insulted by the resolution being sent here. Mr. Hallows : I think it, would be far better if you allowed the matter to drop. Mr. Whitley : The resolution is another shot which has been fired at the Council in an underhanded manner, and is just as much intended as an insult to them as it is to myself. The proposition says Ido not represent the opinion of,the ratepayers or the Parochial Corn- mittee. I fearlessly and emphatically deny that, and repudiate and scorn the imputation conveyed in the pro- , position that I ought to represent nothing but the opinions of the mover, seconder, and sup- ' porter of this resolution, and of those who support the tree planting,many of whom do not live in Stockton Heath and are not ratepayers in the district. I wait. elected by the ratepayers of Stockton Heath and serve them alone and so long as I remain a member of this Council I shall continue, to do so, honestly and truthfully. Mr. Whitley was proceeding with his speech when he was interrupted by the Chairman who intimated that he could not allow him to proceed. Mr. Woodward: Give the matter to the Press privately if you like. I cannot allow you to continue 'here. Mr. Whitley : But I have here a petition signed by 176 ratepayers of Stockton Heath respecting this question. Mr. Hallows : Is this in order ? The Chairman called upon Mr. Whitley to resume his seat. He had heard nothing of the petition and could not receive it that day. The incident then closed.
